Alice Sherwood
Have you visited Digital Commons@TMC, the institutional repository before?Take your research to the next level and learn about the basics of how you can publish your open access student-led (faculty advisor needed) or professional journal on this platform and the steps getting started. item.description:
Srinivasu Mantha

Microlearning, the delivery of content in small units focused on a single learning goal, is increasingly used to build digital competence, yet evidence on its effects on digital literacy and programming ability has rarely been synthesised together. item.description:
Inda Fadila Ainul Hawa, Gina Purnama Insany
Academic information services in universities are still largely carried out manually by administrative staff with limited working hours, making it difficult for students to receive quick responses, especially outside office hours. This study aims to design and implement an academic chatbot using the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach through the Groq API and a Streamlit interface. item.title: What Customers Actually Ask Before Hiring: 112 Real Search Questions Across Five Home-Service and Business-Service Trades (2026)
item.description:
Madison Hoskins
A descriptive field study cataloging 112 real questions customers type into search engines before hiring across five trades — gutter cleaning, gutter guard installation, moving services, handyman services, and AI receptionist services — classified by intent (cost, process, problems, comparisons, local/trust). No search-volume data is claimed.

item.description:
Shuangcheng Sun, Ji Xia
Numerical data and Python scripts supporting “From Document Processing to Research Decisions: Auditing Corporate AI Text Measures”. The package includes saved term counts, paired-report comparisons, reference bounds, verification-task inputs, and replay scripts for the core results. Historical Chinese source comparisons and the ESG application are provided as aggregate outputs only. Licensed raw data, third-party document images, and OCR models are not included. item.title: dvisor: a progressive query engine for the browser
item.description:
Renato Campos Mauro, Eduardo Ogasawara, Cláudio Esperança
dvisor (Data Visualization Optimized Retrieval) is a progressive query engine that runs in the browser. It runs SQL queries against remote Parquet files with no backend server, and streams partial results as they arrive. The engine is written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly.

Winner determination in combinatorial auctions is a weighted set-packing problem and is NP-hard in general. Random Reshuffling (RR) is the default data-ordering strategy in practice, and it is almost always run with minibatches. The recent theory of Liu shows that single-sample RR dominates SGD in smooth convex optimization for every stepsize below \(2/\hat{L}\), but the role of the batch size has not been worked out. Vulnerabilities in Internet-exposed web applications are among the most concrete threats to Internet security: once a flaw is disclosed, attackers rapidly exploit exposed instances at scale—provided they can efficiently enumerate them. item.description:
Maussen, S.
Employees often work under incomplete contracts, performing both contracted in-role tasks and valuable but noncontracted extra-role activities. Once employees have completed in-role tasks, discretionary time remains, which they may allocate to extra-role activities or consume opportunistically. item.title: Deregulation, Market Structure, and the Evolution of U.S. Banking
item.description:
Bisetti, E., Karolyi, S., Lewellen, S.
We construct novel network-based measures of U.S. state-level bank deregulation intensity that allow us to separately identify the effects of deregulation on competition and investment opportunities. In contrast to existing studies, we find that increased competition leads to higher deposit funding costs and a reduction in banks’ net interest margins and profitability. item.title: Redeploying the Jockeys: The Intermediary Role of Venture Capital in Entrepreneurial Labor Markets
item.description:
Hu, Z.
This paper explores how venture capitalists (VCs) add value by examining their role as labor market intermediaries. Using novel data, I show that VCs create internal labor markets (ILMs) to facilitate entrepreneurial mobility across their portfolio firms. Survey evidence suggests that VCs leverage private information about founders’ abilities to strategically match talent to portfolio firms, creating value for the recipient companies. item.description:
Malheiros, I., Poss, M., Subramanian, A., Nesello, V.
The vehicle routing problem with time windows (VRPTW) is a classical problem with many applications. In practice, travel times are time dependent because of traffic and uncertain events, such as accidents, weather, and road work. If these features are ignored, routes planned in advance may become infeasible. Crowdshipping has gained attention as an emerging delivery model thanks to advantages such as flexibility and an asset-light structure. Yet, it chronically suffers from a lack of mechanisms to create and exploit consolidation opportunities, limiting its efficiency and scalability. item.description:
Hao Liang, Solaleh Mohammadi, Kaiqing Zhang
Fictitious play (FP) is one of the earliest and most fundamental learning procedures in games, where each agent independently chooses a best response to the empirical distribution of opponents' past actions by maximizing the expected payoff with respect to it. item.title: FanCyqlone: A Parallelized Solver for Multi-Horizon Optimal Control
item.description:
Matisse Teuwen, Pieter Pas, Mathijs Schuurmans, Panagiotis Patrinos
Multi-horizon optimal control aims to select optimal control sequences simultaneously for several possible future scenarios, ensuring consistency at the first stage. While this enables advanced model predictive control schemes that explicitly handle prediction uncertainty, solving these problems tends to be costly. item.title: Time inconsistent linear quadratic optimal control for mean field games in Hilbert spaces
item.description:
Hongjiang Qian
This paper studies time-inconsistent linear-quadratic mean-field games governed by stochastic evolution equations in Hilbert spaces. The time inconsistency arises through the dependence of the cost functional on the initial time, while the mean-field interaction enters through the mean of the state distribution. item.title: Signature representations of certain BSDEs
item.description:
Peter Bank, Christian Bayer, Marco Rauscher, Marco Rodrigues, Nikolas Tapia
We link the solvability of backward stochastic differential equations with time-augmented Brownian signature data to the solvability of a differential equation on the tensor algebra of signature coefficients. We show that in certain cases the solutions are of closed form and remain within the class of linear functionals of the signature. Lastly, we derive a closed-form solution to a pricing and hedging problem in terms of the time-augmented Brownian signature.

item.description:
Wenqing Ouyang, Andre Milzarek
We investigate when metric regularity of a subdifferential mapping rules out multiple local inverse branches and therefore upgrades to strong metric regularity. Let $h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,\infty]$ be proper, lower semicontinuous, definable, prox-regular, and subdifferentially continuous at $(\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}(\partial h)$. item.title: A Convex-Analytic Reformulation for Poisoning Attacks on Logistic Regression
item.description:
Carina Moreira Costa, Maria Eduarda Pinheiro, Martin Schmidt
We study data poisoning attacks on logistic regression with $\ell_2$-regularization, where an attacker chooses the features of a fixed number of injected observations with prescribed labels to maximize the logistic loss on the clean training data. Strong convexity of the defender's problem yields an exact reformulation through its first-order optimality conditions. item.title: Adaptive Constraint Sampling for Stochastic Gradient Methods in Constrained Optimization
item.description:
Erik Müller, Naum Dimitrieski, Mohamed-Ali Belabbas, Christian Ebenbauer
This paper proposes an adaptive constraint-sampling technique for stochastic gradient-based methods to efficiently solve constrained optimization problems with a large number of inequality constraints. The proposed constraint-sampling technique maintains a set of recently violated constraints and draws the constraint used in each iteration uniformly either from this set or from the set of all constraints. This keeps its per-iteration arithmetic overhead independent of the number of constraints.

item.description:
Long Chen, Jingrong Wei
Accelerated transformed primal--dual (ATPD) methods are proposed for smooth convex optimization problems with affine equality constraints. The methods combine primal--dual dynamics with a transformation designed to accelerate convergence. item.title: Direct Search meets Frank-Wolfe: Inexact Derivative-Free Bilevel Optimization over Polytopes
item.description:
Matteo Pernini, Francesco Rinaldi, Gabriele Sanguin, Marco Viola
In this work we propose BLDS-SIMPLEX, a derivative-free direct search method for the solution of bilevel optimization with polytope constraints at the upper level. The proposed method reformulates the feasible set using barycentric coordinates and explores it using Frank-Wolfe-type directions, relying on a fixed-accuracy black-box oracle for the upper-level objective function. item.description:
Weijian Li, Vince Kurtz, Panos J. Antsaklis, Hai Lin
In this paper, we develop a hierarchical control framework for nonlinear dynamical systems with safety constraints. Specifically, a low-fidelity model is introduced for trajectory planning, while a tracking controller is designed for the high-fidelity system. We first characterize the tracking error bound (TEB) using a storage function. item.title: On the minimum energy required to trigger a spike
item.description:
Guanchun Tong, Rodolphe Sepulchre
We formulate and numerically study the problem of finding the minimum energy required to trigger a spike in a three-dimensional conductance-based excitable model. The variational formulation seeks a state trajectory that reaches the boundary of the spiking region with the least \textit{peak} cumulative work supplied through the membrane port. item.title: Margin-Inducing Optimal Guidance and Control for Atmospheric Entry
item.description:
Emily M. Palmer, Anil V. Rao
A method is presented for margin-inducing optimal guidance and control with application to atmospheric entry. The method induces margin in state inequality path constraints during entry while simultaneously retaining a large portion of the non-margin-inducing performance. The margin in the guidance trajectory is based on a differentiable approximation of the maximum of a continuous function. item.title: An upper bound on the number of edges of a Gomory corner polyhedron
item.description:
A. Yu. Chirkov, S. I. Veselov, D. V. Gribanov, D. S. Malyshev, N. Yu. Zolotykh
We establish the first nontrivial upper bound on the number of edges of a Gomory corner polyhedron, resolving a long-standing open question. For an $n$-dimensional corner polyhedron associated with an integer lattice of determinant $δ$, the number of edges is at most $$ O\left(n6^n \cdot \bigl(1+\log_2(2δ)\bigr)^{2n-3}\right). $$ This improves the standard bound obtained by counting pairs of vertices, reducing the logarithmic exponent from $(2n-2)$ to $(2n-3)$.

item.description:
Hongyan Zhang, Yugang Yu, Qinshen Tang, Ye Shi, Li Chen
Online advertising is a central marketing lever for e-commerce retailers, yet it complicates operational planning by simultaneously stimulating product demand and increasing product returns. Motivated by the practice of a fashion retailer on Amazon, we study a retailer's joint inventory and advertising problem across multiple products over a single season, in which advertising has both direct and cross-product spillover effects on demand and returns. item.description:
Simon Bur{é}, Jona Joachim, Florent Di Meglio
We propose an online method for choosing both a blood pressure target and a norepinephrine dose for an individual surgical patient. From a short record of mean arterial pressure (MAP) and norepinephrine delivery, the method fits a reduced pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model and uses a local Gaussian approximation to propagate uncertainty to future MAP readings. item.description:
Sebastian Debus, Robin Schabert
We study inequalities between symmetric functions that hold in every number of variables. First, we prove that it is undecidable whether a symmetric function with rational coefficients is nonnegative in all dimensions, answering a question posed by Acevedo, Blekherman, Debus and Riener. item.description:
Hossein Nick Zinat Matin
Dynamic time-to-collision (TTC) is the first contact time of a prediction flow and defines a feedback map implicitly. We study its capped value function $\VV$ for Carathéodory dynamics with bounded, measurable forcing. item.description:
